title: Aug 6 Results + Aug 7 Preview: Eight Wins When You Trust the Arms
summary: 8-3 on Aug 6 with 72.7% accuracy. Pirates' bullpen can't hold tomorrow against the Mets.

content.value:
## Aug 6 Recap: The Pitching Matchups Held Up

Eight wins out of eleven games. That's the kind of day that reminds me why we trust the numbers when the arms match up right. From a pitcher's perspective, yesterday was about identifying which rotations had the edge and which bullpens could close it out. We nailed it on 72.7% of our picks, and the three misses? All coin-flip situations or games where variance bit us.

## Breaking Down the Misses

Let me be straight with you—when I see three losses, I look at the confidence levels first. The Orioles pick at 56%? That's barely above a toss-up. Angels got to their bullpen early and capitalized. The Guardians at 50%? That's telling you it's a push. The Royals miss at 62% stings a bit more, but that's baseball. The Twins' lineup got hot at the right time.

What matters is we dominated the higher-confidence plays. The Phillies, White Sox, and Reds picks at 67% all cashed. That's where you make your money—when the model sees a clear pitching advantage.

## Aug 7 Preview: Mets Over Pirates

Tomorrow's top pick is the Mets heading to Pittsburgh, and I like what I'm seeing in this matchup. Zac Thornton gets the ball for New York against Carmen Mlodzinski for the Pirates. At 58% confidence, this isn't a screaming play, but it's a solid pitching edge.

From the mound, Thornton has better command of his secondary pitches and works the zone more efficiently. Mlodzinski can be wild—when you're missing locations in Pirates' home park, a Mets lineup that's patient will make you pay. Pittsburgh's bullpen has been taxed lately too, and if Mlodzinski can't give them six innings, they're in trouble.

content.title: ⭐ Tomorrow's Top Pick - Aug 7
content.sub: Pick: Mets (58%) | SP Edge: Thornton > Mlodzinski

content.value:
## The Pitcher's Take

Here's what I'd be thinking if I'm Carmen Mlodzinski tomorrow: You're facing a Mets team that just got shut down by the Guardians and they're looking to bounce back. They're going to be aggressive early, hunting fastballs, working counts. You can't fall behind 2-0, 3-1 on these hitters or they'll crush you.

Meanwhile, Thornton should be licking his chops against a Pirates lineup that strikes out at a high clip. If he's locating his offspeed stuff—and the data says he has been—Pittsburgh's going to have a long night.

Ride with the Mets tomorrow. Trust the arm that has better control of the strike zone.
